html:
In 1354 an earthquake shook down the walls of Gallipoli, a Byzantine town on the European shore of the Dardanelles, and Ottoman Turks under Süleyman Pasha, son of Orhan, moved in and stayed.

The Ottomans had first crossed into Europe as hired allies of John VI Kantakouzenos in the Byzantine civil war of 1341 to 1347. Gallipoli gave them a lasting base and a safe crossing from Anatolia.

From there they spread across Thrace. They took Adrianople in the 1360s and made it their capital as Edirne. A crusade under Amadeus of Savoy won Gallipoli back in 1366, but the Byzantines handed it back in 1377. Within a century the Ottoman Empire held most of the Balkans and then Constantinople itself.
